ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the outer frame is a square, and the dashed line connects from the upper-left corner of the square to the lower-right corner; it is one diagonal of the square. The bottom side of the square serves as the base of an equilateral triangle, the vertex of the triangle is above and labeled C, and the two slanted sides connect respectively to the left and right endpoints of the base. In the upper-left corner, angle a is located between the left side of the square and the dashed diagonal; in the lower-right corner, angle d is located between the right side of the square and the right slanted side of the equilateral triangle, and angle e is located between the right slanted side of the equilateral triangle and the dashed diagonal. Reasoning: The diagonal of a square forms 45° with each side, so a=45°. Each interior angle of an equilateral triangle is 60°, so the triangle side at the lower-right corner forms 60° with the bottom side of the square. The lower-right corner of the square is 90°, so d=90°-60°=30°. The dashed diagonal forms 45° with the bottom side, while the right slanted side of the triangle forms 60° with the bottom side, so e=60°-45°=15°. Thus d+e=30°+15°=45°=a. Therefore the relationship is e+d=a.

raw_record.question_text: In the figure formed by a square and an equilateral triangle, what is the equality relating angles a, d, and e?

method.method_draft: Numerical angle-measure route. From the image, identify the square, its dashed diagonal from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner, and the equilateral triangle whose base is the bottom side of the square. Angle a is the angle between the left side of the square and the dashed diagonal at the top-left corner. At the bottom-right corner, d is between the right side of the square and the triangle side, while e is between the triangle side and the dashed diagonal. From the text, use that the outer figure is a square and the inner triangle is equilateral. In a square, the diagonal makes 45 degrees with each side, so a=45 degrees. In the equilateral triangle, the side at the bottom-right makes 60 degrees with the bottom side; since the square corner is 90 degrees, d=90-60=30 degrees. The diagonal makes 45 degrees with the bottom side, so e=60-45=15 degrees. Hence d+e=30+15=45=a.

method.method_draft: Parallel-line angle route. From the image, observe that the dashed segment connects the top-left corner of the square to the bottom-right corner. Angle a is formed by the left vertical side of the square and this dashed diagonal. At the bottom-right corner, the angle between the right vertical side of the square and the same dashed diagonal is subdivided by the triangle side into the two labeled angles d and e. From the text, use that the outer quadrilateral is a square, so its left and right sides are parallel. Treat the dashed diagonal as a transversal crossing these two parallel vertical sides. The angle it makes with the left side at the top-left, namely a, equals the corresponding/alternate interior angle it makes with the right side at the bottom-right. Since the image shows that bottom-right angle is exactly the sum d+e, conclude a=d+e.
